questions.question: Water has maximum density at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4°C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Water exhibits a unique physical phenomenon known as the **Anomalous Expansion of Water**. While most substances expand when heated and contract when cooled, water behaves differently between the temperatures of **0°C and 4°C**.
 
• Density is defined as the **mass per unit volume** of a substance. For a constant mass, density is **inversely proportional** to the volume it occupies.
 
• When ice at **0°C** is heated, it melts into water, and the volume actually **decreases** as the temperature rises toward **4°C**. This is due to the collapse of the open **hexagonal crystal lattice** structure of ice.
 
• At exactly **4°C** (more precisely **3.98°C**), water reaches its **minimum volume**. Because the volume is at its lowest, the density reaches its **maximum value** of approximately **1000 kg/m³** or **1 g/cm³**.
 
• Once the temperature rises above **4°C**, the increased **kinetic energy** of the water molecules causes them to move further apart, resulting in standard **thermal expansion** and a decrease in density.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **0°C (Freezing Point)**:

 
 
• At this temperature, water molecules form stable **hydrogen bonds** that create a cage-like structure in **ice**.
 
• This structure makes ice less dense (approx **917 kg/m³**) than liquid water, which is why ice **floats**.
 
 
 
• **100°C (Boiling Point)**:
 
 
• This is the temperature at which the **vapor pressure** of the liquid equals the external **atmospheric pressure**.
 
• At this stage, water undergoes a phase change to steam, and its density drops drastically as molecules become widely separated.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance**:
 
 
• In cold climates, as lake water cools to **4°C**, it becomes heavy and sinks to the bottom.
 
• This process ensures that the bottom of deep lakes remains at **4°C**, allowing **aquatic life** to survive even when the surface is covered in **insulating ice**.

questions.question: Who became the private secretary to Prime Minister Modi in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nidhi Tewari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **March 2025**, the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** officially approved the appointment of **Nidhi Tewari** as the **Private Secretary (PS)** to **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**.
 
• **Nidhi Tewari** is a high-ranking diplomat belonging to the **2014 batch** of the **Indian Foreign Service (IFS)**.
 
• Prior to this prestigious elevation, she served as a **Deputy Secretary** within the **Prime Minister's Office (PMO)**, demonstrating extensive experience in executive administration and strategic coordination.
 
• The role of a **Private Secretary** to the Prime Minister is a critical **bureaucratic position** responsible for managing the Prime Minister’s official engagements, processing sensitive files, and maintaining liaison with various **Union Ministries** and foreign dignitaries.
 
• The appointment is typically made on a **co-terminus basis**, meaning the tenure is linked with the term of the Prime Minister or until further government orders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister's Office (PMO)**:

 
 
• The **PMO** consists of the immediate staff of the Prime Minister and provides secretarial assistance to the head of the government.
 
• It is headed by the **Principal Secretary** to the Prime Minister, who oversees the overall functioning of the office.
 
 
 
• **Sunita Williams**:
 
 
• She is a world-renowned **Indian-origin American astronaut** and a retired **United States Navy officer**.
 
• She holds several records for **spacewalks** and is not associated with the administrative appointments of the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Foreign Service (IFS)**:
 
 
• Established in **1946**, it is the premier **diplomatic civil service** under **Group A** of the Central Civil Services.
 
• Officers are recruited through the **Civil Services Examination** conducted by the **UPSC** and are responsible for representing India's interests in **international relations**.

questions.question: Who was appointed Union Law Secretary in March 2025?

• The **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)**, chaired by the **Prime Minister**, approved her elevation to this prestigious position from her previous role as **Additional Secretary**.
 
• As the **Law Secretary**, her primary responsibilities include rendering legal advice to various Union Ministries, managing **Government Litigation** in the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts**, and overseeing the **Indian Legal Service** cadre.

questions.question: In which year Rajaraja I became the king of the Chola Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**985**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajaraja I**, born as **Arulmozhi Varman**, ascended the **Chola** throne in **985 CE** after the reign of **Uttama Chola**.
 
• His coronation marked the beginning of a new era of **Chola imperialism**, where the dynasty expanded its influence across South India and the Indian Ocean.
 
• He ruled for approximately **29 years**, until **1014 CE**, establishing the Cholas as the most formidable power in the region.
 
• He is celebrated for his military genius, having defeated the **Pandyan**, **Chera**, and **Chalukya** dynasties to consolidate his authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Architectural Marvels**:

 
 
• He commissioned the construction of the **Brihadisvara Temple** (also known as **Rajarajeshwaram**) at **Thanjavur**, which was completed in **1010 CE** and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The temple is famous for its **Vimana** (tower) and the massive monolithic **Nandi**.
 
 
 
• **Naval Supremacy and Expansion**:
 
 
• Under his leadership, the **Chola Navy** became a dominant force, leading to the conquest of the **Maldives** and the northern parts of **Sri Lanka**.
 
• He captured the **Malabar Coast** (Kandalur Salai) to control the lucrative trade routes with the Arabs.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Reforms**:
 
 
• He introduced a highly organized system of **local self-government** through village assemblies known as **Sabhas** and **Ur**.
 
• In **1000 CE**, he conducted a comprehensive **land survey** to streamline revenue administration and taxation.
 
• He was succeeded by his equally illustrious son, **Rajendra Chola I**, in **1014 CE**.

questions.question: In August 2025, ______ launched 'Pratibha Setu' to connect top talent with employers including private sector.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** launched the **Pratibha Setu** initiative in **August 2025** to bridge the gap between high-caliber candidates and diverse employment opportunities.
 
• The portal is designed to provide a platform for candidates who have performed exceptionally well in major competitive exams, such as the **Civil Services Examination (CSE)** and **Engineering Services Examination (ESE)**, but did not make the final selection list due to the limited number of vacancies.
 
• It allows the **private sector** and **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** to access a database of **pre-vetted and disciplined talent** who have already cleared rigorous screening processes and reached the **Interview/Personality Test** stage.
 
• This move aims to optimize human resource utilization in India by ensuring that the country's most **intellectually capable youth** find productive roles in the economy, even outside traditional administrative services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is a **Constitutional Body** established under **Article 315 to 323** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• Its primary mandate is to conduct examinations for appointments to the **All India Services** and **Central Services** of the Union.
 
 
 
• **AICTE** (All India Council for Technical Education):
 
 
• A **statutory body** responsible for the proper planning and coordinated development of **technical education** and **management education** systems in India.
 
 
 
• **UGC** (University Grants Commission):
 
 
• A **statutory body** set up by the Department of Higher Education to maintain **standards of university education** and provide recognition to universities in India.
 
 
 
• **CBSE** (Central Board of Secondary Education):
 
 
• A national-level board of education for public and private schools, focused on the **standardization of secondary education** and conducting **All India Senior School Certificate Examinations**.

questions.question: In Tamil Nadu, ______ is performed by dancers wearing peacock feathers in temples dedicated to Lord Murugan to obtain his blessings.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mayil Aattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mayil Aattam**, also known as the **Peacock Dance**, is a traditional religious and artistic folk dance native to the states of **Tamil Nadu** and **Kerala**.
 
• The dance is specifically performed in temples dedicated to **Lord Murugan**, the Hindu deity of war, as the peacock is recognized as his **divine vehicle** (Vahana).
 
• Performers wear elaborate costumes that include a **peacock beak** and a structural dress adorned with actual **peacock feathers** that can be opened and closed like a fan using a specialized thread mechanism.
 
• A unique characteristic of this dance is that the performers attach **wooden tall pegs** to their feet, requiring significant balance to mimic the **graceful movements**, strutting, and rhythmic hopping of a peacock.
 
• This ritualistic performance is carried out to seek **divine blessings** and is usually accompanied by traditional musical instruments like the **Nadaswaram** and **Thavil**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gambhira**:

 
 
• A vibrant **mask dance** originating from the **Malda district** of **West Bengal**.
 
• It is performed during the **Gajan festival** in honor of **Lord Shiva** and often features solo or group performances highlighting social issues.
 
 
 
• **Pung Cholom**:
 
 
• A unique **Manipuri** classical dance form known as the **Drum Dance**.
 
• It involves dancers playing the **Pung** (a traditional drum) while executing **acrobatic stunts**, high leaps, and rapid spins.
 
 
 
• **Theru Koothu**:
 
 
• An ancient **street theatre** form of **Tamil Nadu**, literally meaning 'street play'.
 
• Performances are usually held during the **Aadi festival** and focus on mythological stories, particularly the life of **Draupadi** from the **Mahabharata**.

questions.question: 'Hareli festival' is celebrated in which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hareli festival** is considered the first festival of the year in the Indian state of **Chhattisgarh**, marking the beginning of the agricultural cycle.
 
• It is celebrated on the **Amavasya** (new moon day) of the Hindu month of **Shravan**, which typically falls during the peak of the monsoon season in **July** or **August**.
 
• The term **Hareli** is derived from the Hindi word **Haryali**, signifying the lush greenery that covers the landscape during this time.
 
• During the festival, farmers offer prayers to their **agricultural implements** such as ploughs, shovels, and axes, as well as to their **livestock**, expressing gratitude for a successful sowing season.
 
• A primary ritual involves the preparation of **Cheela**, a traditional salted pancake made from rice flour, which is offered to the deities.
 
• Young men and children participate in the **Gedi** tradition, where they walk on tall **bamboo stilts** to celebrate the festival and navigate through the muddy monsoon terrain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Assam**

 
 
• Famous for the **Bihu** festivals, specifically **Bohag Bihu**, which marks the Assamese New Year, and **Magh Bihu**, the harvest festival.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh**
 
 
• Known for the **Kullu Dussehra**, a week-long international festival, and the **Minjar Mela** held in Chamba to celebrate the blossoming of maize.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**
 
 
• Recognized for the nine-day **Navratri** festival featuring **Garba** dance and the **International Kite Festival** (Uttarayan) held in January.
 
 
 
• **Ritualistic Significance**
 
 
• In Chhattisgarh, people place **Neem leaves** at the entrances of their homes during Hareli to protect their families from seasonal diseases and ward off negative energy.

questions.question: Which state government has planned to develop Asia's largest jungle safari in the Aravalli hills?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Haryana government** has announced the development of the world's largest **curated jungle safari park**, which will be spread across an area of **10,000 acres** in the **Aravalli mountain range**.
 
• The project is designed to span across the **Gurugram** and **Nuh** districts, significantly boosting the state's tourism potential and contributing to **wildlife conservation**.
 
• At 10,000 acres, this safari park will be five times the size of the **Sharjah Safari Park** in the UAE, which currently holds the record for the largest curated safari park outside Africa with an area of about **2,000 acres**.
 
• The project is a collaborative effort between the **Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** and the **Government of Haryana**, aimed at protecting the ecologically sensitive **Aravalli hills**.
 
• A **Global Design Competition** was initiated by the state to select an international agency for the park's design, focusing on creating a world-class facility for **eco-tourism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aravalli Range Significance:**

 
 
• The **Aravalli Range** is one of the world's **oldest fold mountain systems**, running through **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, **Haryana**, and **Delhi**.
 
• It acts as a **natural barrier** against the eastward expansion of the **Thar Desert** and is a vital **recharge zone** for groundwater in the **NCR** region.
 
• The hills are home to diverse flora and fauna, including **leopards**, **striped hyenas**, **nilgai**, and over **180 species of birds**.
 
 
 
• **Proposed Safari Features:**
 
 
• The park is planned to include ten specific zones, including a **large herpetarium**, an **exotic bird aviary**, and specialized zones for **big cats** (lions, tigers, and leopards).
 
• It will also feature a **botanical garden**, **nature trails**, and an **underwater aquarium** to enhance the educational and recreational experience for visitors.
 
• The initiative aims to prevent illegal **mining** and **encroachment** in the Aravallis by establishing a protected, managed sanctuary.

questions.question: The Kosi Mechi Intra state river link project is associated with which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kosi-Mechi Intra-state Link Project** is a significant water management initiative in the state of **Bihar** designed to divert surplus water from the **Kosi river** to the **Mechi river**.
 
• It is **India's second major river interlinking project** to receive central approval, following the **Ken-Betwa** project.
 
• The project aims to provide irrigation to approximately **2.14 lakh hectares** of agricultural land in the **Seemanchal region**, specifically benefitting the districts of **Purnia**, **Kishanganj**, **Araria**, and **Katihar**.
 
• The **Mechi river** is a tributary of the **Mahananda river**, and this link facilitates the transfer of water from the Kosi basin to the Mahananda basin without the need for large dam construction.
 
• The project is estimated to cost around **4,900 crore** and involves the construction of a **76.20 km** long canal to channel the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kosi River**:

 
 
• Commonly referred to as the **Sorrow of Bihar**, it is known for its unpredictable nature and frequent course changes that lead to catastrophic flooding in North Bihar.
 
• It originates in the **Himalayas** and is an antecedent river that eventually joins the **Ganges**.
 
 
 
• **Interlinking of Rivers (ILR)**:
 
 
• The national perspective plan for ILR was formulated by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** to transfer water from surplus basins to water-deficit basins.
 
• The **National Water Development Agency (NWDA)** is the nodal agency responsible for the feasibility studies and implementation of these links.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh**:
 
 
• Associated with the **Ken-Betwa link project**, which was the first major initiative under the **National Perspective Plan** for river interlinking.

questions.question: What is the gross weight of ISRO's PSLV-XL Configuration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**320 tonnes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** is an expendable medium-lift launch vehicle designed and operated by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to carry payloads to **Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbits (SSPO)** and **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbits (GTO)**.
 
• The **PSLV-XL** configuration is the most powerful variant of the PSLV family, featuring a gross lift-off weight (GLOW) of approximately **320 tonnes**.
 
• This weight is largely attributed to the use of **six extended strap-on motors (PSOM-XL)**, which are significantly larger than the boosters used in the standard PSLV-G variant.
 
• Each of the six **PSOM-XL** strap-on boosters carries **12.2 tonnes** of solid propellant, providing the necessary additional thrust to lift heavier satellites or reach higher orbits.
 
• The vehicle stands at a total height of **44.4 meters** and utilizes a **four-stage propulsion system** that alternates between solid and liquid fuels to achieve high efficiency and precision.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Systematic Stage Breakdown**:

 
 
• **First Stage (PS1)**: Uses an **S138** solid motor containing **138 tonnes** of **HTPB-based** propellant, generating a massive peak thrust for lift-off.
 
• **Second Stage (PS2)**: Powered by the liquid-fueled **Vikas Engine**, which uses **UDMH** (Unsymmetrical Dimethylhydrazine) as fuel and **N₂O₄** as an oxidizer.
 
• **Third Stage (PS3)**: A high-performance solid rocket motor (**S7**) that provides thrust during the upper atmospheric phase.
 
• **Fourth Stage (PS4)**: A liquid stage equipped with two engines using **MMH** (Monomethylhydrazine) and **MON-3** (Mixed Oxides of Nitrogen), allowing for multiple restarts and high-precision orbit injection.
 
 
 
• **Major Mission Successes**:
 
 
• The **PSLV-XL** was famously used for India's first lunar mission, **Chandrayaan-1**, in **2008**.
 
• It successfully launched the **Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)** in **2013**, marking India as the first nation to reach Mars on its maiden attempt.
 
• The variant is also the workhorse for the **NavIC** (Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System) constellation and the solar mission **Aditya-L1**.

questions.question:
Which of the following discovery has been made with AstroSat?

I. The detection of ultraviolet emissions emanating from remote galaxies.

II. The polarisation of X-rays in proximate supernova remnants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **AstroSat** is **India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory**, launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on **September 28, 2015**. It is designed to observe the universe simultaneously in **optical, ultraviolet, and X-ray** wavebands.
 
• Statement I pertains to the discovery made using the **Ultra Violet Imaging Telescope (UVIT)**. AstroSat detected extreme **ultraviolet (EUV) light** from a galaxy called **AUDFs01**, which is located **9.3 billion light-years** away from Earth. This landmark discovery helped scientists understand how the **cosmic dark ages** ended and how the first stars ionized the universe. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• Statement II refers to the capabilities of the **Cadmium Zinc Telluride Imager (CZTI)** payload. This instrument successfully measured the **polarisation of X-rays** from the **Crab Pulsar**, a **supernova remnant** in the Milky Way. This was a significant technical milestone, as measuring X-ray polarisation is extremely challenging and provides deep insights into the **magnetic field geometry** of celestial objects. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **AstroSat** mission carries five distinct scientific payloads:

 
 
• **Ultra Violet Imaging Telescope (UVIT)**: Capable of observing in **Far-UV**, **Near-UV**, and **Visible** bands.
 
• **Soft X-ray Telescope (SXT)**: Employs **Wolter-I grazing incidence optics** to study X-ray spectra between 0.3 to 8 keV.
 
• **Large Area X-ray Proportional Counter (LAXPC)**: Designed for high **time-resolution** studies of X-ray binaries and active galactic nuclei.
 
• **Cadmium Zinc Telluride Imager (CZTI)**: Functions as a hard X-ray detector with **imaging and polarimetry** features.
 
• **Scanning Sky Monitor (SSM)**: Specifically monitors the sky for **transient X-ray events**.
 
 
 
• The satellite was launched into a **650 km near-equatorial orbit** by the **PSLV-C30** launch vehicle from **Sriharikota**.

questions.question: Which IIT is leading the development of the 'Shakti' microprocessor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IIT Madras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shakti** microprocessor project is a significant initiative led by the **Reconfigurable Intelligent Systems Engineering (RISE)** laboratory at **IIT Madras**.
 
• It is recognized as India's first indigenous **industrial-grade microprocessor**, designed to reduce dependency on foreign hardware and enhance national security in the computing domain.
 
• The processor is based on the **RISC-V** (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) open-source **Instruction Set Architecture (ISA)**, which allows for customization without the heavy licensing fees associated with proprietary architectures like ARM or Intel.
 
• Development was funded by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** under the **Microprocessor Development Programme** to foster the **Digital India** mission.
 
• The project encompasses a family of processors tailored for diverse applications, including **Internet of Things (IoT)** devices, mobile phones, and high-performance computing systems.
 
• In **2018**, the first batch of **Shakti** chips, specifically the **C-Class**, was successfully fabricated at the **Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL)** in **Mohali**, marking a milestone in domestic semiconductor manufacturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **AJIT Microprocessor**:

 
 
• Developed by **IIT Bombay**, this is another indigenous processor focusing on low-power, medium-performance applications.
 
• It was designed using the **SPARC V8** architecture and is often utilized in satellite and navigation systems.
 
 
 
• **Shakti Processor Variants**:
 
 
• **E-Class**: A tiny, low-power processor designed for **embedded systems** and smart cards.
 
• **C-Class**: A 64-bit core aimed at mid-range controllers, typically used in **networking** and **storage** devices.
 
• **I-Class**: Designed for mobile, laptop, and **high-end computing** requirements with multi-core support.
 
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat in Electronics**:
 
 
• The **Shakti** project is a cornerstone of the **Self-Reliant India** vision, aiming to create a robust ecosystem for **fabless chip design** within the country.

__
 
• The **BIMSTEC Youth Summit-2025** was successfully hosted in **Gandhinagar**, the capital city of Gujarat, India, from **7-11 February 2025**.
 
• The summit brought together youth leaders and delegates from the seven member states of the **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)**.
 
• The core objective of the summit was to promote **regional integration**, foster bilateral and multilateral relations, and provide a platform for youth to share ideas on leadership, sustainable development, and technological innovation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BIMSTEC Overview:**

 
 
• It is an international organization comprising seven South Asian and Southeast Asian nations: **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **India**, **Myanmar**, **Nepal**, **Sri Lanka**, and **Thailand**.
 
• Established on **6 June 1997** through the landmark **Bangkok Declaration**, its primary goal is to foster rapid economic development and cooperation across diverse sectors.
 
• The permanent secretariat of BIMSTEC is located in **Dhaka**, Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **Other Cities in Context:**
 
 
• **Dhaka:** Serves as the capital of Bangladesh and houses the permanent **BIMSTEC Secretariat**, coordinating regional activities.
 
• **Colombo:** The commercial capital of Sri Lanka, which historically chaired BIMSTEC and spearheaded its science, technology, and innovation sectors.
 
• **Chennai:** A major Indian port city that serves as a key gateway for maritime trade and connectivity projects linking India with Southeast Asian BIMSTEC partners.

questions.question:
In athletics, all running events come under _____.

I. Track events

II. Ground events
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Track events** encompass all running competitions that take place on the specialized **400-meter oval track**, including **sprints**, **middle-distance**, and **long-distance** races. Hence, statement I is correct.
 
• In the official taxonomy of **Athletics** (Track and Field), there is no technical classification referred to as **Ground events**; competitions are strictly categorized into **track**, **field**, **road**, and **combined events**. Hence, statement II is incorrect.
 
• The standard **running track** consists of two parallel straights and two bends, typically made of **synthetic rubber** or **polyurethane** to provide optimal traction for **spiked shoes**.
 
• Events such as the **110m hurdles**, **400m hurdles**, and the **3000m steeplechase** are also categorized under **track events** because they are contested on the running circuit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classification of Athletics**:

 
 
• **Field Events**: These take place in the central area (infield) and are divided into **Jumping events** (High Jump, Pole Vault, Long Jump, Triple Jump) and **Throwing events** (Shot Put, Discus, Hammer, Javelin).
 
• **Sprints**: Short races requiring maximum velocity, typically the **100m**, **200m**, and **400m**.
 
• **Relays**: Team events where four runners carry a **baton**, most commonly the **4 × 100m** and **4 × 400m**.
 
• **Road Events**: Competitions conducted on paved courses, including the **Marathon** (42.195 km) and **Race Walking** (20km and 50km).
 
• **Combined Events**: Multi-discipline contests such as the **Decathlon** (ten events for men) and **Heptathlon** (seven events for women) that test overall versatility.

questions.question: What is the shape of the magnetic field lines around a current-carrying solenoid?

options.text: Parallel straight lines inside the solenoid and concentric circles outside.
Concentric circles centered on the solenoid.
Radial lines extending outward from the solenoid.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parallel straight lines inside the solenoid and concentric circles outside.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **solenoid** is defined as a long, thin loop of wire, often wrapped around a metallic core, which produces a **magnetic field** when an **electric current** is passed through it. It effectively converts electrical energy into magnetic energy.
 
• Inside the solenoid, the magnetic field lines are **parallel straight lines**. This specific geometry indicates that the **magnetic field** is **uniform** in both magnitude and direction at all points within the central volume of the coil.
 
• Outside the solenoid, the magnetic field is non-uniform. Near the individual turns of the **conducting wire**, the field lines form **concentric circles**. These individual circular fields interact and combine to form a pattern that resembles the field of a **bar magnet**.
 
• The **strength** of the magnetic field inside the solenoid is constant, while the field strength decreases significantly as one moves further away from the solenoid exterior.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field is determined by the **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**, where the fingers wrap in the direction of the current and the thumb points towards the **North Pole**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Magnetic Field Strength (B):**

 
 
• **Number of Turns (n):** The magnetic field is directly proportional to the **number of turns per unit length**. More turns result in a stronger magnetic field.
 
• **Current (I):** The field intensity is directly proportional to the amount of **current** flowing through the coil. Increasing the current increases the **flux density**.
 
• **Nature of Core Material:** Using a **soft iron core** inside the solenoid increases the magnetic field strength by thousands of times, creating an **electromagnet** due to high **magnetic permeability**.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnet Applications:**
 
 
• Solenoids are widely used in **electric bells**, **magnetic locks**, and **medical imaging devices** like **MRI scanners**.
 
• They are also essential components in **relays** and **valves** where controlled linear motion is required.

questions.question:
Which musical instrument is shown in the figure given below?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a3975bbc9525b7cd8a16c9ccf52a06f21031d11eca3ceaeb5dcd58444b97791.png]
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jantar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jantar** is an ancient and unique stringed musical instrument belonging to the **Veena** family, primarily used in the **folk music** traditions of **Rajasthan**.
 
• It is distinguished by its construction, featuring **two large resonators** made of **dried gourds** (tumbas) connected by a central bamboo or wooden neck known as the **Dandi**.
 
• The instrument typically consists of **two strings** made of steel and roughly **14 frets** which are often adhered to the neck using wax or resin.
 
• The **Jantar** is played almost exclusively by the **Bhopas**, the priest-singers of **Rajasthan**, while performing the **Phad** (narrative scroll painting) of the folk deity **Lord Devnarayan**.
 
• Unlike many other stringed instruments, the **Jantar** is played while hanging around the neck of the performer with a strap, allowing the musician to **dance** or move during the **ritualistic narration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trumpet**:

 
 
• A high-pitched **brass instrument** used in orchestral and **jazz music**, producing sound through the vibration of the musician's lips on a metal mouthpiece and regulated by **piston valves**.
 
 
 
• **Nadaswaram**:
 
 
• A traditional **double-reed wind instrument** from **South India**, considered a **Mangala Vadya** (auspicious instrument) used in **temples** and weddings.
 
• It is crafted from a dark, hard wood known as **Aacha** and features a **conical bore** ending in a large metal or wooden bell.
 
 
 
• **Mridangam**:
 
 
• The primary **percussion instrument** of **Carnatic music**, it is a **double-sided drum** carved from a single piece of **jackfruit wood**.
 
• Its two heads are made of layered **animal hide** and are tuned to the **tonic note** of the main performer.

questions.question: Which of the following is the use of petroleum gas in liquid form (LPG), a constituent of petroleum?

options.text: Fuel for heavy motor vehicles, electric generators

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fuel for home and industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)** is a flammable mixture of hydrocarbon gases, primarily **propane** and **butane**, which are separated from **crude oil** during the **fractional distillation** process at petroleum refineries.
 
• It is described as petroleum gas in liquid form because these hydrocarbons are gaseous at **standard temperature and pressure** but are easily **liquefied** under moderate pressure for efficient storage and transport in **cylinders**.
 
• LPG is a preferred **clean-burning fuel** for **domestic purposes**, such as **cooking** on gas stoves and **water heating**, because it leaves no residue and has a very high **calorific value** of approximately **50,000 kJ/kg**.
 
• In the **industrial sector**, it is utilized for **metal cutting**, **steam generation**, **food processing**, and as a feedstock for various **chemical synthesis** processes.
 
• Because it is naturally odorless, a pungent-smelling substance called **Ethyl Mercaptan** is added to LPG to allow for the easy detection of **gas leaks**, ensuring safety in homes and factories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paraffin Wax**:

 
 
• A byproduct of the **lubricating oil** fraction of petroleum.
 
• Used in the manufacture of **ointments**, **cosmetic vaseline**, **candles**, **wax paper**, and **polishes**.
 
 
 
• **Diesel**:
 
 
• A heavier petroleum fraction used in **compression-ignition engines**.
 
• Mainly used as fuel for **heavy motor vehicles** like trucks and buses, as well as **electric generators** and **railway engines**.
 
 
 
• **Bitumen**:
 
 
• The heaviest residual component of **crude oil** distillation.
 
• Crucial for **road surfacing** and the production of moisture-resistant **paints** and **waterproofing** materials.
